s1.syndrome_frame: Gastrointestinal bleeding in a patient with a history of cancer and cirrhosis
salient_findings: Gastrointestinal bleeding with two episodes of frank hematochezia
Severe thrombocytopenia with a platelet count of 2,000/µL
key_facts: 60-year-old man
History of squamous cell cancer of the right tongue
History of cirrhosis from hepatitis C
Platelet count 5 days before surgery was 115,000/µL
Underwent right glossectomy with bilateral neck dissection
Hepatitis C with a nucleic acid amplification test result of 1679 IU/mL
Developed gastrointestinal bleeding
Platelet count of 2,000/µL
Prothrombin time is normal
Activated partial thromboplastin time is normal
HIV status is negative
Heparin-associated antibody is negative
Bone marrow biopsy was performed
Cirrhosis of the liver on CT of the abdomen
No active extravasation on visceral angiogram
Approximately 60% infarction of the spleen on post-embolization imaging

shortlist.label: Hypersplenism
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has cirrhosis and splenomegaly, which can lead to hypersplenism, causing thrombocytopenia and gastrointestinal bleeding

shortlist.label: Splenic infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of splenic embolization, which can cause splenic infarction, leading to gastrointestinal bleeding

shortlist.label: Portal hypertensive gastropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has cirrhosis, which can cause portal hypertension, leading to gastropathy and gastrointestinal bleeding

shortlist.label: Esophageal varices
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has cirrhosis, which can cause esophageal varices, leading to gastrointestinal bleeding

shortlist.label: Hemobilia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of gastrointestinal bleeding and has undergone splenic embolization, which can cause hemobilia

raw.rationale: The patient's low platelet count (2,000/µL) and history of cirrhosis from hepatitis C, which can lead to splenic sequestration of platelets, support the diagnosis of hypersplenism. The significant improvement in platelet count is often seen after splenic embolization, which was performed in this case, further supporting this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Splenic infarction
rejected.why: While the patient did have splenic infarction, it was a result of splenic embolization, which was likely performed to treat hypersplenism, rather than the primary cause of the low platelet count.

rejected.label: Portal hypertensive gastropathy
rejected.why: There is no direct evidence of portal hypertension causing gastropathy in this case, and the patient's gastrointestinal bleeding could be attributed to other causes.

rejected.label: Esophageal varices
rejected.why: There is no mention of esophageal varices in the case report, and the patient's bleeding was described as hematochezia, which suggests a lower gastrointestinal source.

rejected.label: Hemobilia
rejected.why: There is no evidence of hemobilia, which is bleeding into the biliary tree, and the patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not support this diagnosis.
